topic: News report: new airport rail link opens
context: The new airport rail link opened to passengers on Friday morning, cutting the journey between the city centre and the international terminal to under thirty minutes. Officials said the line had been planned for more than a decade, with construction delayed twice by land disputes and material shortages. At the opening ceremony, the transport minister said the service would ease congestion on the highway, where average travel times had grown by nearly forty percent in five years. Fares are set at a flat sixty baht for all stations, and discounted cards are available for students and senior citizens. Early-morning trains run every ten minutes, with the first service leaving the city at five thirty. Station staff reported long queues at the ticket machines during the first hour, but said the crowds eased by midday. Transport groups have asked the operator to review the schedule after the first month of operation.

topic: Announcement: road closure for bridge repairs
context: Notice to residents and businesses: Khao San Road will be closed to all traffic from Monday, 22 March, until Friday, 3 April, while crews replace the bridge deck over the canal. The closure is necessary because the current deck has developed cracks that engineers say cannot be repaired without a full replacement. Traffic will be diverted to the side streets, and signboards have been placed at every main junction. Buses that normally pass along the road will use the alternate route and stop at the temporary bus stop near the temple gate. Emergency vehicles will still be able to reach the area at all times. Shop owners on the closed section have been notified directly and will receive a month's reduced rental from the municipality. Residents are asked to plan deliveries and visits in advance and to follow the instructions of traffic staff on site. For further information, call the municipal hotline during office hours.

topic: Advertisement: barista wanted for a downtown café
context: Now hiring: A growing downtown café is looking for a friendly barista to join our team. The ideal candidate is enthusiastic about coffee, enjoys chatting with customers, and is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Previous experience is welcome but not required, as we provide full training on our coffee machine and recipes during the first two weeks. The role involves preparing drinks, serving customers, and keeping the counter clean and stocked. We offer a monthly salary of 18,000 baht, a weekly day off, and a free coffee allowance of two drinks per shift. Shifts run in two teams, morning and afternoon, with rotating weekend cover. Applicants should send a short message describing why they want to work at our café, along with their availability. We will contact shortlisted candidates for a trial shift within one week. Join us and help us grow our little corner of the city.

topic: Business email: order confirmation and delivery details
context: Dear Mr. Tanaka, thank you for your order of three hundred ceramic dinner sets, which we received this morning. We are pleased to confirm that the goods are available and will be prepared for shipment within five working days. The items will be delivered by our courier to your warehouse in Chiang Rai, and you will receive a tracking number by email once the shipment leaves our factory. Please note that delivery will take around seven days, and someone will need to be present at the destination to receive and check the goods. If any items arrive damaged, please send us photographs within three days of delivery so that we can arrange a replacement. Payment terms remain thirty days from the date of the invoice, which you will receive separately. Should you need any further details, please reply to this email or call our sales office during business hours. We look forward to a long and successful partnership.

topic: Article: how the city is preparing for the rainy season
context: Each year, the rainy season brings both relief and challenge to the city. As rainfall arrives, the ground soaks up water, plants turn green, and reservoirs begin to refill after the hot months. Experts explain that a healthy water cycle depends on keeping some rain where it falls, through rooftop gardens, tree planting, and permeable surfaces that let water sink into the soil. This year, the city has widened several drainage channels and repaired old pipes that used to block during heavy storms. Volunteers have also cleaned canals and cleared rubbish that would otherwise slow the flow. Officials warn, however, that no system can prevent every flood, and that residents in low-lying areas should watch weather reports and prepare emergency kits. The key message is that preparation, rather than fear, makes the season easier to manage. Small actions by many households add up to a real difference when the heavy rain comes.
